instructions: About 2 1/2 hours before you want to eat, make the dough. In a small bowl, stir the 2 tsp yeast and 1 tsp sugar into 1 1/2 cups plus 2 tbsp very warm water, about 104°F (40°C). It should feel warm on your wrist, not hot. Leave it for 10 minutes, until it's foamy on top.
In a large bowl, mix the 4 cups flour with 1 1/2 tsp of the salt. Add the yeast water and 1 tbsp of the oil and stir until it comes together in a shaggy dough.

Knead it on the counter for 8 to 10 minutes, until it's smooth and springs back when you poke it. Put it in an oiled bowl, cover it and leave it somewhere warm for about 1 1/2 hours, until it's doubled.
Punch the dough down and cut it into 4 even pieces. Roll each one into a smooth ball, set them on a floured tray, cover and leave them for 30 minutes, until they're puffy.
Meanwhile, make the filling. Finely chop the onion, mince the 2 garlic cloves, and finely dice the red pepper and the tomato. Squeeze half the lemon. That should be about 1 1/2 tbsp of juice.

Heat 2 tbsp of the oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the onion and cook, stirring now and then, until it's soft and golden at the edges, 5 to 6 minutes. Add the garlic and stir for 30 seconds, until you can smell it.
Turn the heat up to medium high and add the 1 lb beef. Break it up with a spoon and cook until there's no pink left and it starts to brown, 5 to 6 minutes.
Add 2 tsp tomato paste, the 2 tsp baharat, 1 tsp cumin, the last 1/2 tsp salt and the 1/4 tsp pepper. Stir for 1 minute, until the paste darkens and the spices smell toasty.

Add the red pepper, the tomato and 2 tsp of the lemon juice. Cook, stirring, until the liquid has cooked off and the mix looks dry, 4 to 5 minutes. Spread it on a plate to cool. Hot filling makes the dough soggy.
Heat the oven to 465°F (240°C) with racks in the top and middle. Line 2 baking sheets with parchment.
Roll each dough ball into an oval about 16 inches long and 8 inches wide. Put 2 on each sheet.
Scatter a quarter of the 10 oz mozzarella down the middle of each oval, then a quarter of the filling on top, leaving a 1 inch border all round.
Fold the long sides in over the edge of the filling. Pinch each end together and give it a twist to make a point, like a boat.
Bake for about 15 minutes, swapping the sheets halfway, until the crust is deep golden and the cheese is bubbling.
Meanwhile, melt the 2 tbsp butter and chop 1/4 cup of the parsley. Cut the other half of the lemon into wedges.
As soon as the pides come out, brush the crusts with the butter and scatter the parsley over the top.
Taste a bit of the filling. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt or a squeeze of the lemon.
Cut each pide across into strips about 1 inch wide. Serve with the yogurt and the lemon wedges, with the red pepper flakes on the side.
advance_prep_notes: start the dough about 2 1/2 hours before dinner so it can rise
method_notes: All three versions roll a yeasted dough into long ovals, fill them with spiced ground meat, onion, tomato and pepper, fold the edges into a boat and bake them hot. RecipeTin Eats (the lead) cooks the filling first with tomato paste, baharat, cumin and lemon, lays cheese under it and bakes at 465°F for 15 minutes; Cooking Orgeous and Chocolates & Chai spread the meat raw with parsley and brush the crust with butter as it comes out. The lead's meat is lamb with beef as its stated swap, so this uses beef, doubles the lead for four pides, and adds the others' butter brush and parsley; Cooking Orgeous's yogurt goes alongside, and its chilli goes on the side to keep the filling mild.
